metadata.title: Global chip stocks rally as Anthropic’s record IPO boosts confidence in AI trade

content.text:
Investing.com -- Global semiconductor stocks rallied Thursday after Anthropic priced the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record, boosting confidence in the AI trade.
In premarket U.S. trading as of 5:49 a.m. ET (10:49 GMT), Micron and SK hynix Inc ADR (NASDAQ:SKHY) rose more than 5%. Intel, Applied Materials, Lam Research and Marvell gained between 4% and 5%.
Advanced Micro Devices added 3.4% and Broadcom 3.2%. Texas Instruments rose 2.5% and NXP 2.2%.
European chip stocks also climbed. AT&S, Aixtron, Siltronic, Infineon and STMicroelectronics rose roughly 3.5% to 8.5%. ASM International and Technoprobe each gained 5.3%, while ASML and BE Semiconductor rose more than 4%.
Anthropic priced its offering at $83 a share, above its marketed range of $70 to $78. It is the largest stock market debut on record and the first by a major developer of frontier AI models.
The company sold 980 million Class A shares, well above its initial plan of 825 million. Of those, 956.35 million came from Anthropic and 23.65 million from selling stockholders, who keep the proceeds.
Investing.com calculations put the offering at $81.3 billion, topping SpaceX's $75 billion debut earlier this year. The deal values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
The company will also raise an additional $26 billion through private placements, it said. Investors agreed to buy 23.6 million shares through a private placement at the IPO price, according to its filings.
Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices are among the private-placement investors, underscoring the chip industry's financial ties to Anthropic as demand for AI computing capacity grows.
Anthropic shares will begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the symbol "ANT."
